scope: Bounded independent review of handoff-only package selection, exact snapshot materialization, deduplicated aliases, line-ending variants, checksum validation and ZIP member names; no frozen model modifications

findings.observed: verify_root accepts missing SHA256SUMS; verify_zip accepts corrupt SHA256SUMS because neither reads its contents.
findings.impact: The delivered integrity utility does not cover one advertised checksum artifact or its manifest binding. Actual package tables independently checked correct.
findings.recommendation: Require exact checksum-table membership and matching digest for every manifested file plus PACKAGE_MANIFEST.json, in both root and ZIP paths.

findings.observed: A fixture modified a retained packaged file after the first build; the second build overwrote it rather than rejecting.
findings.impact: Future use can destroy user edits within a staging tree; no current package-user edit was observed. Old checkout files are not written.
findings.recommendation: Before replacement, require existing target to match previous manifest (or already equal incoming bytes); reject unowned collisions and resolve targets inside stage.

verified_properties: All 6424 frozen inventory files appear in research with committed baseline hashes.
38 line-ending variants are separate from committed primary files.
342 research aliases and 12 runtime aliases resolve to exact bytes; the runtime edition explicitly lacks one nonruntime external reference.
Actual member sets contain no Windows case/trailing-dot collisions, reserved names or resolved paths outside stage.
No node_modules, .git or __pycache__ source trees entered the sealed member sets.
Current SHA256SUMS tables have exact membership and manifest hashes.
Builder copies matching worktree bytes or explicitly pinned Git blobs and never rewrites historical receipts.
current_archive_readback: Root builder owns full every-member SHA readback; this bounded review inspected exact manifest/alias/checksum structures and safe resolved staged paths.
